I have been farming these fields in Quzhou for over forty years. Every year I plant winter wheat in October and follow it with summer maize right after the June harvest — that is what my father did, what my neighbors do, and what I know works on this land. I have about ten mu, which is enough to feed my family and bring in some cash, but not so much that I can afford to take big risks. This spring the wheat looks decent so far, and the soil moisture is about normal, so I will stick with my usual wheat-maize double crop. I am not changing what I grow — why would I? Last year the wheat gave me around 500 jin per mu and the maize did a bit better, so I see no reason to gamble on cotton or vegetables that need more labor and more spraying.

For the wheat, I will rotary till before the next planting season comes around, but right now the wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. I irrigate four times — once at green-up if it is dry, once at jointing, once at heading, and once at grain filling. That is what everyone in the village does. The extension fellow says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, but I have learned that 18 kg gives me a safer yield, so I put down about 50 kg of compound fertilizer as base and topdress with urea at jointing. I also add some phosphate and potash because the soil here needs it, though I do not measure exactly — I know roughly how many bags to spread. For pests and weeds, I spray herbicide once in early spring and insecticide twice, around jointing and heading, to keep the aphids away.

For the summer maize, the window is tight — we harvest the wheat and plant the maize within a few days, sometimes the same day. I use hybrid seed because the yield is much better than the old types, and I do not till again after the wheat; there is no time and the seed drills work fine into the stubble. I give the maize two irrigations, one right after planting to help germination and one around the big flare stage. I put down about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu, usually as a compound fertilizer at planting and a side-dressing of urea later. I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice for the corn borer and other pests. I expect the maize to yield a bit more than the wheat, maybe 550 jin per mu, if the autumn rains come on time.
